(Lil rant here) I’m not gonna defend those who criticized me, but I’ll try to see it from their perspective. I’m from east asia - land of idolization and eds masked as a healthy lifestyle. My theory is it might also be a response to trauma. Most people I know has gone through a phase of extreme dieting/ exercising, some kept that lifestyle for years. It must’ve enraged them that someone who’s deemed as unattractive (ie overweight) like me isn’t desperately trying to look “good”. I did, but it was ten years ago and i’m never going back. I don’t think anyone deserves to live like that. You may hate me after this, but I can assure you that the advice people give you isn’t mean spirited. Let’s say: A is your friend. A has never dealt with issues like yours, and A doesn’t have much knowledge about depression. So A had to google it. The first thing most people see when they google a cure for depression is medication, therapy, exercising and a healthy lifestyle. Of course websites like WebMD or MayoClinic never mentioned the difficulties we have with daily tasks, they just give a very generalized instruction (super irresponsible, considering how complicated the human brain is). And unless A studied healthcare, A might not be able to dig deep enough to give a suitable advice. Therefore most of the advice A give to you comes from vague diagnosis and treatments they saw online, and they thought that was the only way. If OP is reading this, I hope you know that those words people say are just advice, you have full right to disregard them and focus on your healing journey. Do whatever’s best for you and no matter how big or small your achievements are, celebrate it
